archetype: Mardu vampire typal go-wide aggro whose late game is a redundant verified kill-web: four checker-passed two-card infinites arranged as a 2x2 matrix of lose-halves (Vito, Sanguine Bond) x gain-halves (Exquisite Blood, Bloodthirsty Conqueror), an aristocrats layer (Viscera Seer / Cruel Celebrant / Grave Pact) converting free eminence tokens into edicts and drains, Purphoros taxing every cast and Throne of the God-Pharaoh echoing every attack. The engine runs from the command zone via eminence; the infinites are a co-equal plan, not insurance.

role_assignment.default_role: Beatdown, but with real inevitability. The deck owns a piece of the long game — any of four verified loop pairings ends it, and per strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock an unanswerable finisher is a source of inevitability. The deck is not the control deck (29 threat bodies vs 11 removal slots and 1 sweeper), so the honest read is: beatdown that does not fear the game going long, which per strategy:whos-the-beatdown makes overcommitting to the race a misassignment — you may play the value turn a pure racer would skip.
role_assignment.pivot_trigger: Three pivots. (1) Edgar cast (median t6, 51.2% by t6 in goldfish): the alpha-strike window, worth taking because the verified attack turn drains 14/opponent at declare (stack 003) and another 14 at your end step (stack 007). (2) Resolving ANY loop half onto a board that already holds a complementary half — with four halves in the 99, the tutors (Demonic, Vampiric, Diabolic Intent) fetch whichever half completes a pair, per strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors a tutor is effectively a copy of the missing piece. (3) Sequencing choice within the pivot: when both pairings are available, deploy toward Bond+Exquisite (stack 005) — both halves are enchantments, the pairing instant-speed creature removal cannot break (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window: go when the win can't be profitably stopped).

gameplan_by_phase.early_t1_t3: Deploy cheap Vampires on the 8/18/18 curve, bank eminence tokens, leave Edgar in the command zone (the engine is free there). Mulligan on the engine-deck test — enabler-heavy hands beat payoff-heavy ones (strategy:mulligans.engine-hands); a hand of two loop halves and no cheap Vampires is the classic all-payoff mulligan. Herald's Horn on t3 is the best noncreature play: it discounts every subsequent body and digs at each upkeep.
gameplan_by_phase.mid_t4_t6: Layer amplifiers (42.2% by t6) and drain pieces (62.7%) under wrath-math discipline — commit what wins, no further (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math) — but the deck buys resilience rather than restraint: Celebrant/Seer/Grave Pact monetize your own deaths, so a sweeper into this board costs the table edicts and drains. Deploy loop halves with intent: a lone Exquisite Blood or Conqueror reads as value and passively feeds on all table damage; the moment a second complementary half is visible, you are the archenemy (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection).
gameplan_by_phase.late_t7_plus: Take whichever window opens first: (a) Edgar into a protected seven-attacker turn — 14/opponent at declare (stack 003) plus 14 at end step (stack 007) plus counters and combat damage, protection held 57.5% by t6; or (b) tutor the missing half of the most resilient available pairing — Bond+Exquisite if creature removal is the table's held answer (stack 005), a creature pairing only if the coast is genuinely clear. Count open mana before committing and sequence the scariest piece last (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window).

key_tensions: Archetypally telegraphed at bracket 4: Edgar plus any visible half of the four most famous drain pairings in the format (combined combo_details popularity ~355k) means the table plays against the loop from turn zero. The deflection budget (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection) is largely pre-spent by seat assignment; per strategy:threat-assessment you will be ranked by inevitability, not board. Plan for removal on sight of every half and treat deflection as buying single turns, not phases.

Removal-window profiles differ per pairing, and choosing between them is a sequencing skill: stack 005 (Bond+Exquisite) is the resilient line — both halves enchantments, no per-iteration creature-removal window; stacks 001/004/006 each include at least one creature half, and 004/006's own artifacts name the per-iteration instant-speed removal window as the honest cost. When tutoring, fetch toward the pairing the table's open mana cannot answer (strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy inverted onto yourself).

Cheap-deathtouch defense is thin: Vampire of the Dire Moon is the only one-drop deathtouch defender (Nighthawk Scavenger carries deathtouch at three; Bloodthirsty Conqueror has it but is a loop half you should not trade in combat). Kalitas's lifelink-plus-exile body is the compensating anchor. Against fast aggro the control seat (strategy:whos-the-beatdown) is held with drains and edicts more than with blockers.

The infinite is a co-equal plan, not insurance: natural pair assembly 5.4% by t6 / 9.4% by t10 (goldfish, tutors unmodeled), four pairings, three tutors, mana_value_needed 0 on every line. Per strategy:deckbuilding.power-level.barometers this is squarely the bracket-4 profile the report's floor names — play it honestly as such; sandbagging the combo reads as bad faith at this floor, not deflection.

Free-protection tension: Deflecting Swat and Flawless Maneuver are free only with a commander on the battlefield, but the engine wants Edgar in the command zone until the pivot — pre-Edgar, protection costs real mana on the same turns the curve wants for bodies (strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance).

Wrath exposure is partially monetized rather than merely survived: 29 threat bodies invite the sweeper, but Grave Pact/Celebrant/Seer convert your deaths into table damage and selection, and eminence plus Bloodghast rebuild for the cost of the next cast (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math: buy resilience instead of restraint). Purphoros (indestructible, usually noncreature) and the two enchantment halves survive creature wraths outright.

Velocity vs taxes: the 18+18 two/three-drop core is the many-cheap-spells profile that Sphere/Thalia effects punish hardest; under an assembling lock this deck is forced beatdown racing the lock (strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial). Herald's Horn partially rebates a one-mana tax on creature spells — a real but narrow hedge.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Grave Pact edict into Kalitas's exile replacement
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Oracle texts: Grave Pact forces each other player to sacrifice per your creature death; Kalitas replaces opponents' dying nontoken creatures with exile plus a Zombie for you. Plausibly every edict your free tokens generate also denies death triggers/recursion and mints you a body — but the replacement/sacrifice interaction has not been resolved on the record

candidate_missing_lines.title: Aristocrats ignition: Cruel Celebrant death with a full loop pair on the battlefield
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Celebrant's death trigger both drains each opponent 1 and gains you 1 — with any verified pair already on the battlefield, either event should ignite the loop mid-combat or through a wrath. The loops themselves are verified; the ignition-from-a-death path (trigger ordering, which event seeds the loop) is not

matchup_frames.vs_sweeper_control: The wrath costs them more than it costs you: Grave Pact and Cruel Celebrant convert the board they sweep into edicts and drains, the two enchantment halves plus indestructible Purphoros survive, and eminence rebuilds at one token per cast with no recast tax. Still commit only what wins (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math) — but there is no need to fear the long game: against draw-go control your four-pairing inevitability means you may play the patient game they think they own (strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock).
matchup_frames.vs_stax: Forced beatdown: taxes halve the two-spell turns this curve is built on; race the lock's assembly and aim Despark/Fracture/Rite of Oblivion at the piece that beats YOU (strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial). Herald's Horn rebates one mana per creature spell under tax effects. The zero-mana loops are notably tax-resistant once assembled — pieces cost mana, iterations cost none.
matchup_frames.vs_aggro: Take the control seat of the subgame (strategy:whos-the-beatdown) — but honestly note the fair-combat tools are thin: the deck holds one one-drop deathtouch defender (Vampire of the Dire Moon), so stabilization comes from Kalitas's lifelink-plus-exile, each-opponent drains re-taxing the racer's life total, and the gain-halves converting ALL table damage into your life (Exquisite Blood triggers on any opponent's loss, including from other players). You cannot race three life totals; you can make every point of damage anywhere feed you (strategy:combat-math.racing).
matchup_frames.vs_combo: Answer economy inverts: the last profitable moment for held interaction is now (strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy). Your counter-clock is fast — four pairings, three tutors, and 5.4%-by-t6 natural assembly mean the tutored kill is usually one turn away once either half sticks; Deflecting Swat (post-Edgar) and the white removal protect that turn. Against a faster combo seat you are the beatdown and must present the kill first (strategy:whos-the-beatdown).

distribution_notes: 34 lands, 16 enter tapped — a tempo tax; goldfish: land-drop rate 58.2% by t6, mean available mana 5.34 on t6, commander mean cast 6.628 / median 6. Curve 8/18/18/12/6/1 over 63 nonland spells, modal at 2-3, on-template per strategy:deckbuilding.curve. Pips B-dominant: 50 total B pips, source target 36 against 13 B lands plus fixing. Roles (87.6% coverage): 29 threat bodies vs 11 spot/edict/damage removal and 1 sweeper — threat-dense and answer-light, leaning on the table per strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry; sac-outlet 1 (Viscera Seer; Kalitas's ability uncounted by the taxonomy). Ramp-or-fixing drawn 50.2% by t6; drain engine 62.7%, payoff-or-lord 66.3%, protection 57.5%, token amplifier 42.2%, natural infinite pair 5.4% by t6 / 9.4% by t10. Caveats from deck-facts: 12 engine-relevant cards have no role entry (Sanguine Bond, Exquisite Blood, Grave Pact, Anointed Procession among them — absence of role is not absence of function), synergy_graph has 1 intra-deck edge (global shortlist, not a fit score), and no restricted mana in the base.
overall_assessment: This is a beatdown deck with inevitability, and that changes which mistakes are available. The deck plays the game strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry endorses — wide token boards from a zero-mana command-zone engine, each-opponent drains, edicts, and per-cast burn instead of single-target damage — but its long game is not borrowed time: a 2x2 matrix of verified loop halves (stacks 001/004/005/006, all deterministic table-kills) backed by three tutors means the game that goes long is often YOUR game (strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock). The price is paid in perception and in blockers: at a bracket-4 floor with the format's four most famous drain pairings, threat deflection (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection) buys turns rather than phases, and the thin deathtouch wall means fair defense is drains, edicts, and Kalitas rather than bodies. Played correctly the deck presents two genuinely different kills the same table must answer with different cards — a protected 28-per-opponent attack turn (stacks 003+007, composed) and a stack-based loop whose most resilient form is two enchantments (stack 005) — and per strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors the redundancy, not any single pairing, is the deck's real edge.
